paper_label: Injection of Malicious Code into Dependency Tree
asw_definition: Root goal of the attack tree; not used as an individual SWSC attack vector.
mechanism_definition: Root node only. It is not used as a mechanism or attack vector in the Prolog model.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker creates and publishes a new package so that downstream users or tools may adopt it as a dependency.
mechanism_definition: The attacker controls a malicious software artifact that can be consumed by a downstream user or toolchain.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker creates a package that appears useful or benign but contains malicious code.
mechanism_definition: The attacker controls a malicious software artifact that can be consumed by a downstream user or toolchain.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker creates a package name based on common spelling mistakes or small variations of a legitimate package name.
mechanism_definition: The attacker controls a software artifact that appears related to, or can be mistaken for, a legitimate artifact.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker reuses an abandoned or withdrawn project, package, or account identifier to deliver a malicious package.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can redirect or control a software reference that downstream users or tools rely on.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker compromises an existing package that already has users, contributors, or maintainers.
mechanism_definition: The attacker gains control over a legitimate software artifact or its release path.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which malicious code is inserted into the source code of an existing package.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can modify source code that will later be consumed, built, or executed.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker submits a malicious pull request that appears to be a benign contribution.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can modify source code that will later be consumed, built, or executed.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker commits malicious code using maintainer-level authority.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can modify the legitimate project source code with trusted contributor or maintainer privileges.

asw_definition: An account-compromise attack in which weak, stolen, or exposed credentials/API tokens are used to gain maintainer-level access.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can act through a legitimate account and use its permissions to modify, build, or distribute software artifacts.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker manipulates project trust relationships to obtain maintainer status.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can modify the legitimate project source code with trusted contributor or maintainer privileges.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which malicious code is introduced during the build process rather than directly in the source code.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can influence the build process or build output.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker compromises resources used by the build system, such as compilers, plugins, proxies, or DNS services.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can manipulate the build infrastructure used to produce software artifacts.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker manipulates dependency/package downloads during the build process.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can manipulate the channel through which software artifacts are retrieved.

paper_label: Run Malicious Build on Shared Systems
asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker abuses shared build infrastructure so that malicious resources affect another project’s later build.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can execute or trigger a build process that produces a malicious software artifact.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which malicious code or malicious package versions are introduced through the package repository or hosting system.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can manipulate the package-hosting infrastructure used to store or serve software artifacts.

asw_definition: An account-compromise attack in which weak, stolen, or exposed credentials/API tokens are used to publish malicious package versions.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can act through a legitimate account and use its permissions to modify, build, or distribute software artifacts.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker exploits vulnerabilities in a package repository or hosting system to affect package contents or releases.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can manipulate the package-hosting infrastructure used to store or serve software artifacts.

asw_definition: An attack vector in which the attacker places malicious package versions in an alternative repository or mirror and waits for victims to retrieve them.
mechanism_definition: The attacker can redirect or control a software reference that downstream users or tools rely on.

asw_definition: trigger_definition
Root goal: malicious code executes after it is already present in the dependency tree.
candidate_M: Not A_sw; this is execution/trigger behavior.

asw_definition: Malicious code executes during package installation, often through install logic such as package manager scripts.
candidate_M: Useful later for explaining downstream consumption.

asw_definition: Malicious code executes when package test routines are run.
candidate_M: Useful if a VLSI flow runs tests or validation scripts.

asw_definition: Malicious code executes when the downstream package or program runs and invokes the malicious logic.
Malicious code executes only when selected conditions are satisfied.
candidate_M: Useful for evasion or target-specific attacks.

asw_definition: Malicious code checks application state before executing.
candidate_M: Example: production mode, wallet balance, resolvable domain.

asw_definition: Malicious code checks whether a specific dependency or package is present.
Malicious code checks the operating system before executing.
